news.title: New Zealand select squad for first FIFA U-15 Boys World Cup in Azerbaijan
news.lede: New Zealand Football have named their squad for the inaugural FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival, starting in Azerbaijan this month. The squad includes six players from Wellington Phoenix, three from Auckland United, two from Christchurch United and one each from Nomads United, Bay Olympic and Fencibles United. Unlike traditional FIFA age-group tournaments, the competition will use an eight-a-side format, with matches comprising two 20-minute halves. The team will be coached by Wellington Phoenix’s head of boys’ talent development and men’s U-18 head coach, Cam Grieve.

news.title: Fifa to offer extra £2.6bn for football development
news.lede: Fifa president Gianni Infantino will be standing for re-election in March. Fifa is set to propose a $3.4bn (£2.6bn) increase in the amount of money it hands out for football development across the world. World football's governing body wants to release the money from its reserves in a move which would more than double the level of planned distribution funding for 2027-2030. It says it has been able to release the extra cash because of the commercial success of this summer's World Cup.

news.title: Morocco Women to Face France in Friendly Ahead of 2027 World Cup
news.lede: Rabat - Morocco's women's national team is set to face France in an away friendly scheduled for Saturday, December 5. The game takes place at the Auguste Bonal Stadium in Sochaux, kicking off at 9:10 PM GMT. Both squads will use this encounter to test squad depth and refine their game plans ahead of major upcoming competitions, most notably the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup in Brazil. For both sides, the fixture offers a valuable opportunity to evaluate player readiness and fine-tune strategy ahead of official tournament play.

news.title: ParaMatildas hunt more Australian football history at World Cup
news.lede: Eloise Northam will be representing the ParaMatildas at her third IFCPF Women's World Cup. (ABC News: Daniel Irvine). The ParaMatildas are looking to defend their IFCPF World Cup title in Atlanta after winning the 2024 tournament. The Pararoos are also searching for a breakthrough top-10 finish in the men's competition.

news.title: Tessa Wullaert: Helping girls in Belgium find their place in grassroots football
news.lede: The Belgium captain knows what it takes to reach the top. She is now using that experience to support the next generation through grassroots football. As her country's all-time leading scorer, the first Belgian player to reach 100 international goals and the first Belgian woman nominated for the Ballon d'Or Féminin, Tessa Wullaert has already secured her place in European football history. But alongside her own achievements, the FC Como Women player is increasingly focused on where the next generation's journey begins – grassroots football.

news.title: Unity EURO Cup: Mahmoud’s story
news.lede: Syrian refugee Mahmoud Ali explains how football helped him to connect with people in his new home in Germany. Now he supports other refugees through the same organisation that helped him. In Syria, Mahmoud Ali only played football at school and for fun, but after he arrived in Germany in late 2015, the sport quickly became a huge part of his life. It was only through participating in open football training sessions with Berlin-based organisation Champions ohne Grenzen (Champions Without Borders) that he was able to find a sense of community and friendship.

news.title: Morocco opens museum for Jewish culture in Arab World
news.lede: Local media said the exhibition galleries explore communal institutions, including synagogues, Hebrew schools, and rabbinical courts. The new Museum of Moroccan Jewish Culture opened its doors in the city of Fes on Monday, marking the first time in history that an Arab-Muslim country has allocated public funds to establish a museum entirely dedicated to Jewish culture. According to Morocco's National Foundation of Museums, the 1,700 square meters space invites visitors on a journey into the heart of Moroccan Jewish life and Judaism through a rich and diverse collection of ritual and everyday objects, archaeological, ethnographic and artistic artifacts, archives and rare manuscripts, crafts, traditions, as well as practices and testimonies handed down through the 2500 of Jewish history in the country.
